answer: Because the age is read from the terrace checkpoint rather than self-declared, the yarrow audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the comet ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm therefore means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. That is 22 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
